title: Main goes green: an MP4 exported twice stops reading 7 levels apart on GitHub's runner
goal: Main's checks went red on 2026-11-22 because a test that exports one recording twice found the two pictures 7 shades apart where it allows 6, on GitHub's shared machine, after three tries. Make the check tell the encoder's own wobble from a real change so main goes green, without loosening what it guards (a picture that really changes).
notes: Repro: gh run view 44998427631 --log-failed (commit 6d4e30f90, a queue-only commit, so app code unchanged from the green run 44995299075 before it). Output: '✘ Test "Exporting the same recording twice gives the same file to look at" recorded an issue at VideoExportBudgetTests.swift:354:9: Expectation failed: (worst.apart → 7) <= 6'. The test already retries 3 times and keeps the closest pair (8e6b4769d); 2026-10-27 GitHub read 7 vs 6 once before. Options: compare a small average over the frame rather than one squeezed pixel, or a tolerance of 8 with a separate gross-change check. Filed by the long-edit perf task's pass 26 (main red, not its code).
acceptance: The test 'Exporting the same recording twice gives the same file to look at' passes on three CI runs of main in a row
A real change in the exported picture (for example one frame dropped or a colour shifted by 20 levels) still fails it, shown by a test or a written run

log.note: Triage 2026-11-22: moved p1 to p2 and re-tagged unmanned-loop (it is the check machine's health, not video speed). Ran the command in the notes: gh run view 44998427631 --log-failed shows the failure as written (worst.apart 7 <= 6, VideoExportBudgetTests.swift:354). It is intermittent: main went green on the next two runs (45014627531, 45019449805), and the last time this test read 7 was 2026-10-27. That is roughly once a month. Real, but not top of the queue while main is green.

Reproduction: could not get a 7 on this Mac, and found why the check is fragile. Measured (temporary experiment test, removed) two exports of the 2s busy source at 0.2/1.0/1.8s: the hardware encoder alone, quiet or with five exports beside it, read 0 to 1 on the old one-pixel sample but single pixels up to 33 levels apart; the software encoder alone was byte-identical; a hardware write against a software write (the fallback HardwareEncoder.start takes when the hardware is full) read single pixels up to 31 apart and the old sample 2. The old colour(of:) draws the frame into 1x1 at low interpolation, so it reads about one pixel and lands on encoder wobble at random: GitHub's 7 is that. On the average of each 32 pixel square the same pairs read at most 1.83; one frame later reads 16.5 to 17.7; red +20 reads 20. Chose 32 pixel squares with the bar kept at 6 over raising the one-pixel bar to 8, because the squares separate wobble from change by a factor of 8 while a one-pixel bar of 8 would still sit inside the 20-33 single-pixel wobble.

Shipped 42e9102a2: VideoExportBudgetTests.twiceIsTheSameFile compares patches(of:atSeconds:) (32px square RGB averages) via PictureGap, bar samePictureLevels = 6, retry kept. New test aChangedPictureReadsFarApart: a real export with frame 29 cut out reads 16.4 at 1.5s against the whole export, red +20 reads 20.0, frame against itself 0; both must exceed 12 (twice the bar). Scripts/test.sh exit 0 (full suite, 2026-11-22).
owns no walks; the ones it names are examples

Shipped 42e9102a2: the export-twice test now compares the average colour of each 32 pixel square of the frame instead of one squeezed pixel, bar still 6 levels. Measured locally: single pixels wobble 20 to 33 levels between two writes of one file (hardware under load, hardware vs software), squares at most 1.8; one dropped frame reads 16.4 and red +20 reads 20.0. New test 'A picture that really changed reads far apart' proves both still fail the bar on real exports. Scripts/test.sh exit 0. GitHub CI run 45049403395 on 42e9102a2 green on three attempts in a row (1, 2, 3), the export-twice test passing in each.
